en: I take refuge in Tripurasundarī, who wanders in the Kadamba groves; who is like a cloud to the flock of sages; whose hips surpass the mountains; who is served by celestial women; whose eyes are like fresh lotuses; who is dark as a new rain-cloud; and who is the consort of the Three-Eyed Lord. (1)

I take refuge in Tripurasundarī, the consort of the Three-eyed Lord; she who dwells in the Kadamba forest, who holds a golden lute, who wears a necklace of great jewels, whose face shines with the beauty of wine, who manifests the power of compassion, whose eyes are pure and wide, and who moves gracefully. 2.

We have been playfully shielded by some woman who is dark as a rain-cloud; she possesses a braid like a *kadamba* grove, a necklace shimmering upon the weight of her breasts, and breasts that rival mountains; she is one whose tides of grace are heavy, whose cheeks are flushed with passion, and whose speech is skilled in sweet song. (3)

I take refuge in Tripurasundarī, the consort of the Three-eyed Lord, who dwells in the midst of a Kadamba forest, seated upon a golden pedestal; she who resides within the six lotuses, who is like the ever-perfect lightning, whose luster mocks the hibiscus flower, who wears the blooming moon as her crest-jewel. 4.

I take refuge in the daughter of the sage Mataṅga, who plays the lute gracefully upon her breasts, who is adorned with curling locks of hair, who dwells upon the lotus-bed, who hates those of crooked minds, whose eyes are reddened by passion, who deludes even the enemy of the Mind-born (Śiva), and who speaks with sweet words. ||5||

I take refuge in Tripurasundarī, the consort of the Three-Eyed Lord; she who first blossomed with the flower of youth, whose garment is dark blue like drops of blood, who holds a small vessel of honey, whose outer corners of the eyes roll with intoxication, who is elevated by the weight of her firm breasts, whose topknot has loosened, and who is dark-complexioned.

During the rite of recitation, I meditate upon Ambikā, who is anointed with saffron and kissed by *amlaka* fruits; whose eyes are accompanied by gentle smiles; who holds a bow, arrows, a noose, and a goad; who deludes all people; who is adorned with red garlands, ornaments, and garments; and who is radiant as the *japā* flower. (7)

I worship the Mother of the World, the handmaid of the celestial brides—the wife of Purandara, who acts as her hairdresser; the devoted wife of the Grandfather (Brahmā), whose garments are shimmering with fine silk; she who adorns herself with the jewels of Mukunda’s beloveds. (8)
Thus ends the *Tripurasundarī-aṣṭaka*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
